title: Semistable Galois alteration over a complete trait
statement:
A trait is $\operatorname{Spec}R$ for a Noetherian local domain of dimension one with principal maximal ideal. It is complete strictly henselian if $R$ is complete for that ideal, is henselian (simple roots of monic polynomials over its residue field lift), and has separably closed residue field. Its canonical log structure is $\mathcal O\cap j_*\mathcal O_\eta^\times$, where $j$ includes its generic point. Mixed characteristic means fraction-field characteristic zero and positive residue characteristic.

Let $S$ be a complete strictly henselian mixed-characteristic trait, and let $X$ be an integral regular scheme flat and quasi-projective of finite type over $S$ [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Quasi-projective over a scheme $B$ means admitting a locally closed immersion into some $\mathbf P^n_B$; projective means a closed immersion into some $\mathbf P^n_B$ followed by projection [def-kun-projective]. There exist a finite group $G$, a finite dominant trait extension $S^{\prime}\to S$ with $S^{\prime}$ complete strictly henselian, and an integral regular scheme $X^{\prime}$ quasi-projective of finite type over $S^{\prime}$ and over $S$, with a $G$-equivariant commutative square $X^{\prime}\to X$, $S^{\prime}\to S$. The action on $X,S$ is trivial, $a:X^{\prime}\to X$ is projective dominant, and there is a nonempty open $U\subset X$ on which $a^{-1}U\to U$ is a connected finite etale $G$-torsor [def-sbc-normal-dominant-galois]. The scheme $X^{\prime}$ has semistable reduction over $S^{\prime}$: etale locally it has charts etale over $\operatorname{Spec}R^{\prime}[t_1,\ldots,t_n]/(t_1\cdots t_r-\pi)$, where $1\le r\le n$ and $\pi$ is a uniformizer. Its divisorial fs log structure, trivial on the generic fibre, is $G$-stable, log regular [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], and log smooth over the canonical log trait $S^{\prime}$ [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]. No restriction on the degree $\#G$ is asserted. Finite means affine with module-finite coordinate algebras [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism].

from.place: Proof Step 3: dimension-normalized Verdier duality, regular finite-torsion local model; pointwise purity and composition used to compare the normalized curve with the ambient regular scheme. Input: Gabber purity for a regular Noetherian closed pair. More precisely: Expose XVI, section 3.7 second paragraph through its last paragraph, printed pp.254--255: semistable G-alteration, ell-Sylow H, tame equivariant modification, quotient over T=S prime/H, and log resolution. Geometric construction only, before applying Theorem 3.6.2 and Proposition 3.5.7; preliminary finite extension to normalize constants in the first paragraph. Specifically: XVI 3.7, the preliminary constant-field preparation and the four-bullet semistable G-equivariant square.
